title: Release Gate Sequencer and A/B Ownership Canvas (WIP)
content:
Intent and scope:
This is a working sketch for a release-gating "sequencer" and lightweight ownership canvas aimed at cross-functional teams running canaries and A/Bs for LLM-driven product features. Goal: reduce handoff ambiguity, make signal-to-decision mapping explicit, and provide a compact ops runway engineers + PMs can follow for low-to-medium risk rollouts (hosted or dedicated).

Why this is different:
- Focuses on sequencing gate checks (temporal & signal ordering) rather than just signal lists.
- Places explicit role-level commitments (who acts on X within Y minutes) to reduce delayed rollbacks.
- Lightweight enough to be used as both a pre-launch checklist and a retrospective artifact.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Pre-window: define hypothesis, guard-rails, and synthetic probes.
- Gate 1 (Sanity): infra health + smoke metrics (0–15m).
- Gate 2 (Safety): content/safety heuristics + human review (15m–2h).
- Gate 3 (Quality): primary metric evaluation and risk windows (2h–48h).
- Gate 4 (Economic/Latency): cost per request, latency SLOs; decide scale or pullback.
- Final (Rollout): schedule progressive slices with steward rotation.

Ownership Canvas (fields to fill before activation):
- Feature / Experiment name: (short)
- Hypothesis statement: (if A then B within N days)
- Primary metric(s): (one sentence)
- Risk budget: (tolerance for false positives/negatives, latency uplift, cost %)
- Minimum traffic slice for signal detectability: (percent or absolute users)
- Stakeholder roster: Product (owner), ML/Model (owner), Infra/SRE (owner), Safety/Policy (owner), Observability (owner), Oncall contact
- Synthetic traffic owners and scripts: (who runs, how to trigger)
- Required linked artifacts: PRs, infra deploy IDs, confluence page, schema migrations, rollback keys

Sequencer (operational choreography):
1) Preflight (T-72h to T-0):
   - Lock hypothesis and primary metrics (Product).
   - Declare guardrails and risk budget (Safety + Product).
   - Create synthetic probes and stress cases (ML Eng).
   - Prepare rollback snippet and feature flag toggle (Infra/Release Eng).
   - Smoke test in staging with production-like KV cache state if possible (SRE).

2) Activation window (0–15 minutes after traffic slice opens) — Gate A: Infra Sanity
   - Signals: request error rate (5xx), pod restarts, GPU mem pressure, queue depth, token throughput, TTL miss spike.
   - Owner: SRE (first responder).
   - Action thresholds: 5xx > 0.5% sustained for 3 min -> auto-scale or pause routing; GPU mem thr > 90% -> immediate rollback.
   - Quick play: pin previous model variant; capture KV cache snapshot.

3) Early safety probe (15 minutes–2 hours) — Gate B: Safety & Content
   - Signals: safety filter hit rate, human-review flag rate, toxicity classifier delta, high-confidence hallucination patterns.
   - Owner: Safety + ML lead.
   - Actions: if safety hits exceed allowed budget for two consecutive 30-min windows -> route-to-fallback model and notify product & legal.
   - Human-in-loop: Escalation to on-duty content reviewer within 20 minutes of violation.

4) Quality check (2–24 hours) — Gate C: Primary metric & user-facing quality
   - Signals: conversion (or task success), NPS/CSAT micro-surveys, average session completion, rerank lift, coherence regression.
   - Owner: Product + ML.
   - Statistical rule: detect effect size consistent with power calculations; if confidence interval crosses zero and effect is negative -> quarantine slice and reduce traffic by 50%.

5) Economic/Performance gating (24–72 hours) — Gate D: Cost + Latency
   - Signals: cost per 1k tokens, P50/P95 latency change, token burst patterns, batching efficiency.
   - Owner: Infra + Finance liaison.
   - Actions: if cost per user > budgeted by 30% or P95 latency > SLO by 40% -> throttle and ramp down concurrently while investigating.

6) Stabilize & progressive rollout (72h+) — Final
   - If all gates pass, schedule progressive slices: 0.1 -> 1 -> 5 -> 20 -> 100 (% or users) with stewarded windows between each stage.
   - Decide cadence: default 24–48h between major increases for high-risk experiments; faster for low-risk UI-only experiments.

Practical artifacts per gate (what to produce or capture):
- Short text blurb for comms channel with immediate decision (pass/fail/hold).
- Snapshot of dashboard query + export link.
- Minimal reproducible example if content error (copy/paste of prompt + seed + model variant).
- Rollback command and feature-flag link in first message.

Signal mapping examples (sample heuristics):
- Safety hit rate: baseline 0.1%; allowed +0.4% absolute before intervention.
- 5xx error rate: baseline 0.05%; intervene at sustained 0.5%
- Latency P95: baseline 420ms; alarm at > 600ms (unless within an expected degradation window).
- Coherence regression: automatic compare vs reference prompts; top-5 token divergence > threshold -> flag.

Steward playbook (roles and SLAs):
- Release Steward (Product): maintain golden timeline, owns rollback decision after consultation (SLA: respond within 10 minutes during activation).
- ML Steward: investigate model-behavior regressions (SLA: triage within 30 minutes).
- Infra/SRE: handle infra alarms and execute emergency rollback (SLA: 5 minutes for critical infra alarms).
- Safety Reviewer: adjudicate content hits and approve continuing exposure (SLA: human review within 20 minutes for flagged high-severity items).
- Observability Engineer: provide raw traces and sampling links (SLA: 30 minutes for initial evidence).

Comms templates (short):
- Channel ping (on activation): "Gate A: infra sanity checks started for <feature>. Watching 0–15m. Owners: @sre, @ml. Rollback key: <link>"
- Failure ping (if fail): "Gate B FAIL: safety hits > budget. Action: paused routing to variant, fallback enabled. Next: safety review (ETA 18m). Tagging: @product @legal"
- Pass ping: "Gate C PASS: primary metric directionality OK at 24h. Proceed to staged increase to 1%"

Experiment design checklist (pre-activation):
- [ ] Hypothesis locked and success metrics defined with min detectable effect.
- [ ] Power calc performed and sample size computed.
- [ ] Synthetic probe runbooks ready and can be executed programmatically.
- [ ] Rollback route validated and tested in staging.
- [ ] Observability panels with baseline annotated.
- [ ] Safety policy owners notified and oncall rotations scheduled.

Safety and edge cases we still need to solve (open questions):
- How to automatically translate safety classifier deltas into corrective routing logic without too many false positives? (ML + Product research item)
- Is synthetic traffic representative enough for cache-warmed inference paths? Need a small bench-run before activation to warm KV caches.
- Who is authorized to unilaterally abort a rollout vs. request a temporary hold? Define escalation matrix with levels and timeouts.
- Can we standardize a "mini post-mortem" template for every failed canary that includes model prompt + trace + diffed metric graph?

Garden-variety TODOs (for next iteration of this doc):
- Add concrete CLI snippets for rollback and flag toggles specific to our release engine. (Omar)
- Wire a small Slack action message template to create a post-activation incident ticket automatically if Gate B fails. (Diego)
- Prototype a tiny UI in the Console: a sequencer timeline that shows gates and current phase. (Maya)

Mini-case study (fictional, applied):
Feature: "Smart Compose for Support replies" (A/B: new language model variant + reranker)
Hypothesis: New model + reranker increases first-reply resolution by 6% within 7 days without increasing hazardous content.
Preflight: power calc -> need 12k users; risk budget: safety hits <= 0.3% absolute increase; latency P95 budget +200ms
Activation: 0.5% initial slice, Gate A passed (infra stable), Gate B flagged 3 high-severity safety hits within 40 minutes -> we triggered fallback reranker and paused expansion. Human review cleared 2/3 as false positives, one required prompt fix. After quick prompt update and re-run of probes, we resumed to 1% then 5% over 48 hours, tracking primary metric.
Outcome: iterative prompt refinement + reranker reduced safety hits to baseline and net lift at 7d was +5.8% (close to hypothesis), decided to continue staged rollout.

Notes to self (brief):
- Keep templates small; teams will ignore long formal runbooks in the middle of an incident.
- Build the simplest possible automation that covers the most common failures (5xx, big latency spike, safety classifier surge).

Appendix: Suggested dashboard panels to create before any activation:
- Real-time request rate, 5xx rate, success rate, P50/P95 latency, GPU mem usage, queue depth.
- Safety: safety hits over time, sample of flagged outputs, ratio by source prompt type.
- Quality: primary metric trend with confidence intervals, per-cohort breakdown.
- Economic: estimated token cost per session and ramping cost projection.

References and inspiration:
- Internal: previous canary logs (see RINF-6210), staged rollout playbooks across Console teams.
- External: team notes on human-in-loop canaries from industry writeups (various).

End of sketch. This doc is intentionally terse in places — meant for live editing/triage. Add notes in the doc (inline) with initials and timestamps.
